content.speaker: Bertolt
content.text: Hello, gentlemen.

content.speaker: Resident I
content.text: Hello, comrade of Zeno.

content.speaker: Resident II
content.text: Comrade.

content.speaker: Resident II
content.text: If you're here to see Comrade Evgeni, we can wait a little. Or is there something else important you'd like to discuss?

content.speaker: Bertolt
content.text: We talked, and Ms. Windsong was there.

content.speaker: Resident I
content.text: Comrade Evgeni is doing what's best for everyone, we all know that. But I'll tell you, I personally don't want to leave this place. Even if he ...

content.speaker: Bertolt
content.text: No, the lady turned down my proposal. And Comrade Evgeni didn't seem too invested in it either.

content.speaker: Bertolt
content.text: Isn't Zeno's help good news for all of you?

content.speaker: Bertolt
content.text: I can't comprehend the reasoning behind rejecting an abundance of food, a suitable climate, and comfortable housing.

content.speaker: Resident I
content.text: It's not easy to leave something you've built with your own hands, comrade. I doubt you've ever experienced living in a home you built yourself, let alone living in this way!

content.speaker: Resident II
content.text: Chances are you have never even touched freshly mined ore in your life!

content.speaker: Bertolt
content.text: That's true, gentlemen. But why do you insist on doing everything yourself?

content.speaker: Bertolt
content.text: It seems that our conversation has come to an end. I will stay here until Evgeni arrives and gives an answer, which should be soon.

trails.title: United Hands
trails.description: Dealing with these neighbors is something everyone is familiar with, but having an extra person around is always beneficial.

content.speaker: Patrik
content.text: Identical long tables, matching chairs, and potatoes, potatoes, and more potatoes.

content.speaker: Patrik
content.text: In the past, we had access to tin cans and even jam and flour. It was a challenge to transport supplies, but fortunately the weather was cold enough that nothing spoiled during the trip. Time was not an issue in those days, we had an abundance of it.

content.speaker: Patrik
content.text: The little ones used to come and ask for Alenka. While we couldn't indulge their every whim, a treat now and then was fine. Being too strict does no one any good.

content.speaker: Patrik
content.text: Had I known the true value of Alenka, I would have been more careful about giving them away. Maybe I could have kept a few. Oh well, too late to regret now.

content.speaker: Patrik
content.text: At first, we gathered around a single table to portion out the canned food, meticulously sopping up every last drop of broth. But now, there are more tables, but a lot less variety in our meals. And it's not like we can go hunting for critters to supplement our meals.

content.speaker: Patrik
content.text: Why can't people live off ore like they do?

content.speaker: Patrik
content.text: I have an urge to give a detailed account of my past and present experiences because Rayashki is exceptional; it is the most remarkable town I've encountered, although my travels have been limited.

content.speaker: Patrik
content.text: But I'm worried that it will one day disappear.

content.speaker: Patrik
content.text: That's for sure. If Comrade Evgeni agrees to Zeno's proposal, this place will soon be a land of snow again. The factories, the machines, everything will be covered with snow, just as it was when we first arrived ...

content.speaker: Patrik
content.text: I have to remember to write down all the details in case the kids ask me. I want to be able to tell them about everything that disappeared. Of course, it's not going to be written down in any textbooks ...

content.speaker: Patrik
content.text: There are countless unsung heroes in Rayashki, a place filled with ordinary people just trying to make ends meet. That's the reality of our lives here.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: It's me.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Oh, you!

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: I want to talk.
Hotel, Rayashki

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I was just about to look for you, Comrade Evgeni. I've found more details!

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Here.
Windsong turns away and begins to search through the mountainous piles of documents.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Trust me, they will ease your mind, more or less.
A cold wind rushes between them through the open window.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: Let's skip to the point.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: I want you to stop your research.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: Our exploration has only just started, yet many of our people have already been hurt.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: Can you promise there won't be further injuries, or worse, before we've found this fairy-tale treasure?

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: Your so-called new resource is still unconfirmed, yet the price we've paid looking for it is already mounting. We had other options, safer options for all of us.
The snow has turned to wet rain; it splashes up from the windowsill and on to her as they speak.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: We just need to be better prepared. We will arm ourselves with more knowledge for next time.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: I know what you're after here: the study of ley lines, right?

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: The people here may be enthusiastic, but they are only laymen. I've spoken with someone who can help you far more.
The unhurried steps of expensive boots mark an unfortunately familiar guest.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: It is good to see you, Ms. Windsong.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Our proud scholar of a budding, if still informal, school.
His expression is genuine and surprised, as though this is the first time they've ever met.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: And you, the Big Shot from Zeno. Should I feel flattered you stopped by?
He feigns obliviousness to Windsong's teasing.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: I read your files, as Mr. Evgeni suggested.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: You know already that Zeno has investigated many arcane cases and been deployed to many places related to arcanum, but we have never met anyone quite as obsessive in their study as you are.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: What now? Have the big shots decided they are going to trust my studies?
Bertolt smiles. He always smiles, brimming with all the joy of a crocodile.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Well, while I might admire your perseverance myself, no, they're not convinced.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: We just wonder what you and your school have gained from this long journey?
He looks past her, assessing the mounds of scattered papers.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Enough with the crap.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: As you wish. First, I believe you owe Comrade Evgeni some thanks.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Huh?
A fresh letter of recommendation is handed to Windsong.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: The less than satisfactory results from your study may not have earned this letter from Zeno, but Comrade Evgeni insisted on us offering it to you.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Once you have our recommendation, you will be able to communicate with all the renowned scholars in our lab. Your long wait for recognition will be over. A once-in-a-lifetime opportunity.
His tone is calm. His victory is assured.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: All I ask is stop this farce.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Heh!

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Well, I am so grateful. I think I might cry.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: All we have to do is wait for Zeno's grace to be bestowed on us. We should be moved to tears by your mercy, no?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Putting aside your sarcasm, I would suggest you consider the danger of throwing away this opportunity.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: You are wasting time, effort, maybe even lives on some foolish wild goose chase. We can offer the people here a much safer and more feasible way forward. Don't you see?
Bertolt raises an eyebrow. He presents his case less as reason than as indisputable truth.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: And what about Rayashki?
He looks at her pitifully.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: All things come to an end. It will disappear quietly, overtaken by the wilds of this land, when the time comes.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: At least, it may leave a small place in the historical records.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: No offense intended, Mr. Evgeni.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: We cannot solve the problems we're having without Zeno's help.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: All of these problems will be solved as long as we find this new resource.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Ahem! I'm afraid you're mistaken, Ms. Windsong.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: As far as Zeno is concerned, the value of this land is exhausted, fairy-tale resources notwithstanding. Once we've transferred the arcanists away, Rayashki will be abandoned.
The crocodile smile cracks again, growing annoyed at his now long-overdue victory.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: We are aware of the danger that staying here poses to these people, and it is our responsibility to save them. Whether they wish to resist us or not. That's the only reason for our decision, understand?
Windsong sets down the ley energy chart, the culmination of her countless efforts, without saying a word.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Let's be practical.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Zeno has many outstanding young people, a strong academic atmosphere, a better future. You will get your opportunity to revive your school of ley lines, if you pass the exam.
Her fingers press onto the paper, tracing a newly embossed seal.
The "carrot" is sweeter and more fragrant than before.
How long now had she imagined this moment?
In dim, stuffy basements, in underpaid editorial offices, under faceless, nameless, scrutinizing gazes.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: This will be a better choice for all of you.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Haha.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Mr. Big Shot, could you use your rusted brain to think of a more noble reason than consumerism and elitism?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Do you really think our desire for a better life is the only reason why we refuse to leave?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: You used ordinary people as a stepping stone to power and privilege, and even now you take our sacrifices for granted.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Reality is cruel: not you, not Rayashki, and not even Zeno can save everyone. You will have to deal with that.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: You should take what is to come as an inevitable optimization of our society's development.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I know. Life may still get harder even if we find this new resource.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: So what?
The defiance in her voice reignites her long-lost courage.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Your brand of elitism may have invaded every corner of the world, but not this town, not yet.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: I see, most scholars like you hold the same naivete.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: They refuse to leave any of their "comrades" behind, even if the price is their own future.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: What we would sacrifice ourselves for is not the study of ley lines, or any other personal goals.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: But our dream to thrive together!

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: To live in a bright future we all can share!

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: As for this ...
She scrunches up his gaudy recommendation.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I don't need it.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: *spits* A leopard never changes its spots.
Bertolt leaves his final words hanging in the room, departing without looking back.
The crumpled letter rolls out of the window. It lands in the snow, slowly being covered until there is no trace of it left.
Will things get better?
Windsong, too preoccupied to care, slumps back in her chair, gulping in the crisp air of her new world.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: I envy your innocence, Ms. Windsong.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: For many years, I believed that our mission was to change the world.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: But when I looked up, the gate to the new world was already closed. Little Rayashki just coasted along, and I tried to keep everything the way it was.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: But I failed.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: Rayashki is doomed. All our efforts, our will, our dreams—nothing can change the creeping reality. We attempted to achieve something meaningful, something that could make history, but ...
Evgeni strains to lift his head, his face obscured in a kind of darkness beyond the reach of light.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: The spirit of the times stands against what we are building here, not just Zeno, but the whole world.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: That's what reality is like: boring, cruel, disappointing.
The scene falls into a wordless, motionless quiet.
After a long while, Windsong rises.
She has shed all other burdens, and the tantalizing carrot is gone.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: You are too pessimistic, Comrade Evgeni.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: Huh?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Zeno has tried to recruit me several times. Do you know what I've learned from all their efforts?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: They don't want us to explore that mine.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: They belittled our efforts, offered pity for Rayashki, and then planned out a promising future for us.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Yet they didn't give us a hand, even when our people were injured or died.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Do you really think they are so eager to stop us just because they don't want any more sacrifices?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Of course not, my friend.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: A lesson I learned from living in their society ...

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Never do what your enemies want you to do.
She grasps his shoulder, giving it a shake to pull him up to his senses.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Zeno is afraid of us.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: They are afraid that we may discover a new kindling to relight our fire, that we may burn so brightly that we grow out from their control to create our own future.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: You ...

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: But they can't have it their way. Rayashki belongs to us, as does the future!
Faint flickers of that fire seem to be there, somewhere in the man before her.
Evgeni looks up with a complex expression.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: I, I will give it some thought, Ms. Wi- ... Comrade Windsong.
